newsitem.title: USA: Northwest Airlines confirms Airbus talks.
newsitem.headline: Northwest Airlines confirms Airbus talks.

text.p: Northwest Airlines Corp, the fourth largest airline in the world, confirmed it is in talks with European consortium Airbus Industrie but declined to discuss details of those talks.
"We are in talks with Airbus," Jim Faulker, Northwest Airlines, spokeman said commenting on a published report that Northwest has tentatively ordered up to 40 jetliners from Airbus.
Separately, Paris-based Airbus confirmed the talks but declined further comment.

An airline industry source, who asked not to be named, however, confirmed that Northwest is talking to Airbus about ordering up to 40 A-330s. These planes could replace some of Northwest's existing wide-bodied aircraft, the source said.
If all of the 40 are ordered, the total value of the order could be up to $4.2 billion.
Faulkner said Northwest has previously ordered 16 Airbus A-330s jetliners which seat about 300 passengers, and 20 Airbus A-320s which seat about 150 passengers.
Last year, Minneapolis-based Northwest took delivery of the last of 16 new Boeing 757 jetliners which seat about 180 passengers.

At least half the planes covered by the preliminary agreement are firm orders, with the balance identified as future-purchase options, according to a report in the March 18 Wall Street Journal citing people familiar with the negotiations. The order is expected to be finalized and announced in two to three weeks, the report said.
Airbus is a consortium comprising state-owned Aerospatiale of France, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG, and Spanish Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA).
